state.case_summary:
A man in his 70s with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and moderate pulmonary hypertension presented with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling. He reported recurrent palpitations that occurred randomly and were often associated with shortness of breath. His medications included aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, tiotropium, and a budesonide-formoterol inhaler.

No specific physical examination findings were detailed in the case report.

- Echocardiography: Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% compared with 60% 2 months prior.- Cardiac Catheterization: 25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery.- Telemetry and ECG Findings:  Image Title: Figure 1. Initiation, Termination, and Reinitiation of Tachycardia  Image Description: Shows initiation and termination patterns of tachyarrhythmia. In sinus rhythm, RR interval 800ms, PR interval 200ms. First PAC PR interval 200ms, second PAC with prolonged PR interval of 390ms.  Image Title: Figure 2. Electrocardiogram  Image Description: Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with rate of 120 beats per minute. Shows subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia.
